title: Ventura builds new mile-long sand berm to protect vulnerable coastline ahead of El Niño winter storms - ABC7 Los Angeles

 Ventura builds new mile-long sand berm to protect vulnerable coastline ahead of El Niño winter storms 
 Ventura is building a sand berm to protect its coastline from winter storms. 
 By Sid Garcia Tuesday, November 17, 2026 8:21PM 
 Ventura is building a 6-foot-high, nearly one-mile sand berm to protect coastal homes, businesses and roads from large waves and winter storms. VENTURA, Calif. (KABC) -- The city of Ventura began building a nearly mile-long sand berm on Monday to protect coastal properties and infrastructure from large waves and storms forecast for the winter rainy season.
 Once completed, the berm will stand about 6 feet high along a vulnerable stretch of the coastline. Officials said it is designed to safeguard nearby apartment buildings, homes, businesses and roads.
 Crews worked as powerful waves pounded the shoreline amid an ongoing High Surf Advisory. The waves did not cause any major problems on Monday, but officials are preparing for additional storms forecast around Thanksgiving and a Super El Niño expected during the rainy season.
 “With the Kelvin waves, and the high tides and the high surf, obviously, you’ve seen the bigger waves,” said Mary Joyce Ivers with Ventura County Public Works. “They’re coming up farther onto the beach, and so it could cause a lot of damage, and we’re trying to protect our infrastructure.”
 Mack Douglass with the Ventura Police Department’s Emergency Services said the area could face a significant coastal flooding threat during high tides.

 “On those high-tide days, we would be at a pretty high coastal flooding risk without any surf at all,” Douglass said. “With a moderate winter swell in the 4- to 5-foot range, we could see major impacts without something like this berm here.”
 The Ventura Pier remains closed because of the large, crashing swells.
 The berm is expected to be completed on Tuesday, with the goal of protecting nearby buildings from large surf expected over the next several weeks.
